indicators.note: follows tells us the agreement word comes after the compiler's contraction

parts.note: the compiler speaking of himself says 'I am', contracted to I'M
an understanding between parties is a pact or agreement

explanation.surface: A solver muses that grasping a clue's sense depends on what the setter intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The compiler's' is crossword shorthand for I'M (the setter is 'I'); 'follows' puts PACT after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact can mean significance or force of an idea, so the import or meaning of something.

parts.note: hip means fashionable, which is in
to have received something is to have got it

explanation.surface: Someone with a hip injury was given some small metal rods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' is not anatomy but trendy, IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast blocks of gold or other metal are bars, typically oblong.

indicators.note: turned means the concealed run is read backwards
about says the letters lie around within the words, hidden across them

explanation.surface: Elegant flight attendants spin round and lose their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: The run DESSESSOP spans 'stewardesses, sophisticated' and is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone possessed is crazed as if by a demon, hence frenzied or mad.

indicators.note: involved in places the edges word inside the swindle word

parts.note: a con is a swindle, cheating
the lips of cups or holes are their rims

explanation.surface: Red lipstick worn by a con artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of the colour red.

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
criminal behaviour is lawless, disregarding the law

explanation.surface: A villain who somehow has a spotless record.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect and unmarked has no flaw, so it is without any blemish.

indicators.note: protecting means the log wraps around the new letter

parts.note: a felled tree trunk is a log

explanation.surface: A trunk sheltering a young conifer sapling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' is not a tree but a verb, yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to yearn or ache for it.

clue.text: Heartless roughneck accepted by female labourer

indicators.note: accepted by means the woman takes in the ends of roughneck

parts.note: a female person is a woman

indicators.note: heartless strips away the inner letters, leaving only the ends of roughneck

explanation.surface: A cruel oil-rig hand taken in by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A roughneck is an oil-rig worker, which tempts you to read 'labourer' into it; only its ends are used.
explanation.definitionFit: A manual worker is a labourer, especially one in a trade.

indicators.note: in puts I and caught inside the time-period word

parts.note: a season or period of time is an era
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: I picked a bloom at a certain time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, which bear small flowers.

clue.text: Sun exploit employing birds results in excited anticipation

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

indicators.note: employing means the use word takes in the birds

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: Using birds to harness solar energy leads to great excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan, a convention worth knowing; 'results in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense uncertainty while waiting for an outcome is anxious, excited anticipation.

clue.text: Go on spilling secrets, invading privacy initially

definitions.text: Go on spilling secrets, invading privacy initially

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A busybody chatters on, revealing confidences and prying into people's private lives.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-in-one: the whole clue describes a tattler, while GO plus the first letters of 'spilling secrets invading privacy' builds the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who chatters on and spills others' secrets is a tattler or scandalmonger by nature.

clue.text: Crazy Lear isn't showing what's inside

indicators.note: crazy suggests the letters of the words that follow go wildly out of order

explanation.surface: King Lear, in his madness, refuses to reveal his inner feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' rearranges LEARISNT; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts or intestines are the internal organs, literally the contents of a body.

clue.text: Eloquence over Right by Cameron perhaps

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
by in the sense of per, as in so much a day, gives A
David Cameron, former Conservative prime minister, is an example of a Tory

explanation.surface: Fine speechmaking from the right wing, such as that of Cameron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' gives A as in 'so much a head'; 'perhaps' marks Cameron as one example of a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of public speaking and persuasive rhetoric is eloquence.

indicators.note: endlessly means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: to care for a patient is to treat them
a sure friend is a faithful, reliable one

explanation.surface: An owner devotedly looks after a loyal animal forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims TREAT to TREA; 'pet' is a term of endearment rather than an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherished person, someone called a darling or precious one, can be addressed as a pet.

parts.note: a mischievous troublemaker is an imp; the possessive just links
ale is a kind of beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone laces the drink belonging to a mischief-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like doping a drink, but it means pierce with a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike is to pierce or skewer something on a sharp point.

indicators.note: carrying means I and S hold the rearranged drug between them

parts.note: one is the numeral I, and the 's gives S

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something unsound, so the letters of opium are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain is carrying some suspect opium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives both pieces of the holder: the numeral one and the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking reverence for God is irreligious, which can extend to sinful or wicked.

indicators.note: spreading suggests the letters are spread about and rearranged

parts.note: here the possessive S counts as a letter, giving all of UNCTIONS

explanation.surface: Someone smearing on ointment, apparently aiming to be oily about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' rearranges UNCTIONSAIMSO, thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous describes oily, smugly pious manners, a close synonym for holier-than-thou.

clue.text: Performance of pantomime ends in speech

indicators.note: in puts the end letters of pantomime inside the speech word

parts.note: a formal speech is an oration

indicators.note: ends asks for the outside letters of pantomime

explanation.surface: A pantomime show finishing with someone's address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performance' looks like the show itself, but it is the definition, in the sense of working; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The running or working of a machine or process is its operation, its performance.

parts.note: a gig is a musical performance
anti means against
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A grand concert in opposition to nightclubs, with the ellipsis running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge or enormous in size is great in the sense of very big.

clue.text: Eat dinner with time unusually vague

indicators.note: unusually means the letters are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Having an evening meal at an odd hour, an imprecise one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges EATDINNER together with TIME; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not fixed or settled is uncertain, hence vague or imprecise.

indicators.note: in puts the wholly word inside the drawn-games word

parts.note: drawn games are ties
all means wholly, entirely

explanation.surface: Following on, the games all end level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' is a verb, corresponds, not games.
explanation.definitionFit: If one account corresponds with another it agrees or matches it.

clue.text: Drink for everybody, including company, on house

indicators.note: including means the all word holds the other pieces

parts.note: everybody is all

indicators.note: on means placed above, so company comes first in this down entry

explanation.surface: Free booze for all, firm included, courtesy of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the house' suggests free drinks, but 'on' only stacks company over house in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits, beer and wine are drink, intoxicating liquor.

clue.text: Where holy man gets appropriate covering

definitions.text: Where holy man gets appropriate covering

indicators.note: covering means the appropriate word wraps around the saint

parts.note: the very thing is exactly the appropriate one
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A clergyman puts on suitable robes somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: An all-in-one: the whole clue also describes the church room where clergy put on robes; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This church room is where the priest dons vestments, the proper covering for a service.

clue.text: Whack! Old man returning strikes with disgust

indicators.note: returning means the words for whack and old man are read backwards together

parts.note: a whack is a slap
one's old man is one's father, pa

explanation.surface: A father hits back with a slap and a look of revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' covers both the whack and the old man, read backwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: To horrify or dismay someone is to fill them with disgust, so strike them that way.

clue.text: More natural expression of pleasure, embracing sweetheart

indicators.note: embracing means the cat's sound wraps around the centre letter

parts.note: a contented cat purrs
the heart of sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A contented sigh while hugging a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' read as 'heart of sweet' gives E, not a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Less adulterated or unmixed, closer to its unspoilt state, is more natural.

clue.text: Tea's found in neat container to buy

indicators.note: found in says the tea goes into the neat word
container marks the word for neat as the one holding the other

parts.note: neat spirits are undiluted, pure
cha is slang for tea; the possessive supplies the S

explanation.surface: A shopper buys a tidy caddy with tea inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is old British slang for tea, from Chinese; 'neat' means undiluted, as of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase as a verb is to acquire something by paying, a formal synonym for buy.

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of eat

explanation.surface: A dog starts to eat a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' looks like a fish but is the verb, smoke-preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To kipper fish is to preserve it by salting and smoking, a way of treating food.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: The clock runs down at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges TIMERUNS; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal station or final point of a route is its end.

clue.text: Tory leader's hard disagreement on economy

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of the word Tory

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a rift is a disagreement or breach between people

explanation.surface: The Conservative chief has a bitter quarrel over economic policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful use of money is economy or frugality, sound housekeeping.

clue.text: Church increased time being consumed to baptise

indicators.note: being consumed means time is swallowed inside the word for increased

parts.note: prices that have increased have risen

explanation.surface: A church where attendance grew, with services running long, before a baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a name at baptism is to baptise, its everyday synonym in church ritual.

indicators.note: in places the short language word inside the gutted say
gutted means say loses its middle, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: LANG is the short form of language

explanation.surface: Someone casually says 'gutted' in clipped colloquial speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech full of colloquial, casual words is informal in register.
